name: navigate_device
description: Start turn-by-turn NAVIGATION on the user's own phone (or tablet/XR device) in ONE shot. Use this for 'navigate me to X', 'take me to X', 'give me directions to X', 'send this address to my phone', 'start navigation to the job site' — including an address you just read out of a calendar event or an email. It fires ONE deterministic Android navigation intent over Tailscale, so Google Maps opens directly in turn-by-turn mode on the device: no screen watching, no tapping, no on-device model, sub-second. Prefer this over control_device whenever the goal is simply to START navigating somewhere — control_device drives the whole UI with a slow multi-step loop and is only needed when the task is more than 'navigate there'. The destination is free text (a street address, a place name, a business, or 'lat,lon') and the maps app geocodes it itself, so pass the address through verbatim — do NOT try to look up coordinates first. If the request is SCHEDULED or UNATTENDED (a cron job, a morning briefing — the phone will be locked in a pocket), pass delivery='notify' so it arrives as a notification the user taps: Android will not let this open Maps by itself from the background.

destination.description: Where to navigate to, as free text — a full street address ('1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA'), a place or business name ('CN Tower', 'Home Depot Ancaster'), or coordinates as 'lat,lon' ('37.4224,-122.0841'). Passed to the maps app verbatim; it does the geocoding. Do not invent coordinates for a named place.

device.description: Optional target device name (tailnet hostname or MagicDNS name) — targets ANY device on the tailnet. Omit for origin-aware routing: the device the request came from, else the operator's designated PRIMARY device. Naming a device that is not this operator's origin is never a silent retarget — it must be an explicit target here.

mode.description: Optional travel mode. Omit to let the maps app use the user's default (usually driving). Turn-by-turn navigation has NO transit mode — if the user asks for transit/public-transport directions, say so rather than substituting another mode.

avoid.description: Optional route restrictions — a comma-separated subset of 'tolls', 'highways', 'ferries' (e.g. 'tolls,ferries'). Omit for no restrictions.

app.description: Optional navigation app: 'google maps' (default), 'waze', 'osmand', 'organic maps', 'here', an explicit Android package id, or 'any' to let the phone's default handler take it. Only set this when the user names an app — omit otherwise.

delivery.description: How the navigation reaches the screen. 'auto' (the default, and right almost always) lets the phone decide: it opens Maps immediately if the app is in the foreground, and posts a tappable notification if it isn't. 'notify' ALWAYS posts the notification — choose it for anything SCHEDULED or UNATTENDED (a cron job, a morning briefing, a reminder fired while the user is asleep or driving), because the phone will be locked in a pocket and Android silently refuses to let an app open Maps by itself from the background. 'direct' forces the immediate launch and is only safe when the user is holding an awake phone right now — it is the wrong choice for a scheduled run. Read the RESULT before you describe what happened: a notification is NOT a started navigation.

returns: On success, data.delivery says which outcome ACTUALLY occurred — 'direct' (Maps is open and guiding now; data.navigating true) or 'notify' (a notification is waiting on the phone and NOTHING is navigating until the user taps it; data.awaiting_user_tap true). Never describe a 'notify' result as started navigation. Also data.delivery_requested, data.delivery_confirmed (false = an older device build that didn't state its outcome), data.device, data.destination, data.mode, data.avoid, data.app, data.task_id. On failure, a structured data.error_kind: invalid_argument / no_device / no_primary_device / invalid_target / origin_mismatch / lost_contact / not_authorized / bad_response / maps_missing / unsupported_device / invalid_destination / declined / background_blocked (Android refused a background launch — nothing is navigating) / notifications_blocked (the device won't allow the notification, so there is nothing to tap) / unsupported_delivery (the device rejected or could not confirm the requested delivery) / device_error.
example: navigate_device(destination="1247 Main St W, Hamilton, ON", mode="driving", avoid="tolls")  ·  scheduled/unattended: navigate_device(destination="1247 Main St W, Hamilton, ON", delivery="notify")
notes: One-shot, not a loop: the executor resolves the target with the same origin-aware rule as control_device (mesh.resolve_device — explicit device -> the originating device, which must belong to this operator -> the operator's PRIMARY device) and POSTs a SINGLE {msg:'action', type:'intent', name:'navigate', params:{destination, mode?, avoid?, package?}} frame to that device's Tailscale listener (:8765 /action). No screenshot, no ReAct loop, no control session, no on-device model. The device fires a google.navigation: deep link, which is real turn-by-turn — it starts guidance immediately rather than just showing a map (use control_device or the show_map intent if the user only wants to LOOK at a place). Wire contract mirrors IntentActions.kt exactly: mode is the google.navigation letter (d driving / b bicycling / l two-wheeler / w walking — there is NO transit letter) and avoid is a duplicate-free subset of 'thf'; the friendly words here are mapped in _MODE_CODES/_AVOID_CODES/_APP_PACKAGES. A cloud-originated push is confirm-gated ON THE DEVICE (ActionOrigin) — a declined prompt comes back as error_kind 'declined'. DELIVERY (M3, docs/plans/2026-07-24-location-context-and-navigation.md): params.delivery is ALWAYS on the wire, 'auto' included — unlike mode/avoid/package it is never omitted, so a device build can never read an absent key as 'legacy caller, launch directly'. 'auto' is resolved ON THE DEVICE because only it knows whether it is foreground. The device states the outcome back in its action_result: an explicit delivery:'direct'|'notify' if present, else its fixed success detail phrase ('started navigation' = direct; anything naming a notification/queue = notify) — docs/schema/action_result.json pins additionalProperties:false with a CLOSED error enum, so that phrase is the only channel it has today. MEASURED DEFECT this closes: with the app backgrounded, targetSdk-36 Background-Activity-Launch restriction discards startActivity WITHOUT throwing, so M2 returned success:true and Maps never opened; a user tap on a notification is the documented BAL exemption. Because of that, a device that returns success for a 'notify' request without stating a notification is reported as error_kind 'unsupported_delivery', never as a success — an unverifiable claim is the bug, not a nicety.
